title: Phenotypic Signature of a Molecular Element Can Be Used to Understand Its Function
content: An outstanding issue in molecular biology is understanding the function of elements (e.g. transcripts, CpG sites, and metabolites) detected by high throughput screening platforms. In this study an analysis plan was devised to construct the phenotypic signature of an element by integrating its QTLs with GWAS data. By applying this plan to categories of (un)known transcripts, through a two-step discovery and validation, I provided evidence that the phenotypic signature is a robust metric and it can be used to infer the function of an unknown transcript. In the manuscript, I detailed the analysis plan and the procedure to infer the function of a molecular element. The computed database of phenotypic signatures and the related scripts are publicly available.
